questions.prompt: GTA 6 is everywhere tonight — and the talk isn't just the story, it's the size of the world waiting behind it, side streets and all. Which scene sounds most like yours tonight?

options.text: Locked in — main story first, I've already got my route planned.
Already wandering in my head — side streets first, the story can wait.
My brain's racing through everything I want to do first.
Too much world at once — the map's so big I don't know where to start.

questions.prompt: Phoebe Bridgers lit up SNL — and the clips are still glowing tonight, that slow-burn kind of performance that stays in the room. When a song hits like that, where does it pull you tonight?

options.text: Leaning all the way in — letting every note land, slow and full.
Sending it to someone right away — a song like that is meant to be shared.
Turning it up — the glow is the whole night now.
Too tired to feel it tonight — the glow's there, I'm just running on empty.

questions.prompt: GTA 6 is coming, and everyone's already arguing about the same thing: when the world finally opens, do you follow the main story — or ignore it and wander off into everything else? Tonight, with the wait still on, which way are you leaning?

options.text: Straight down the main story — I'm finishing what they built first.
Side streets first — the story can wait, I want to see everything.
One thing at a time, no rush — I'll wander when I feel like it.
Stuck choosing — too many directions, I keep starting and stopping.

questions.prompt: The SNL glow is still in the air, and tonight's turning into a slow Phoebe Bridgers listen — songs on low, lights down. If someone handled tonight's wind-down drink for you, what would you want in your hand?

options.text: Chamomile, slow and warm — unwinding one sip at a time.
Virgin or hard — a spiced cider with a little kick, made for a glowing night.
Something sparkling and cold — easy sipping while the playlist rolls.
Just water, I don't need anything else tonight.

questions.prompt: Phil Collins stood up at the Rock Hall and told the crowd: you haven't heard the last of me — and the line is still echoing tonight. What does a comeback like that sound like to you?

options.text: Like the opening drums rolling back in — a comeback you can feel in your chest.
Like a quiet return — just him, steady, no need to prove anything.
Like the old favorites on repeat — songs I already know by heart.
Like a spotlight that won't let up — everyone's watching to see if he still has it.

questions.prompt: The Oak Ridge Boys' ten essential songs are making the rounds tonight — the kind of classics that have been playing for decades. In the hour ahead, how do you want it to feel while the old favorites play?

options.text: Easy — let the songs roll one after another, no skipping.
Steady — settled in, the classics doing what they've always done.
Curious — digging for the deep cut I forgot I loved.
Fading — the songs are just background while I wind down to nothing.
